title: CRUD Operations
learning_outcomes: Explain what crud operations contributes to a PHP application.
Apply at least one of these concepts in a small example: create records.
Check one edge case and explain how to diagnose unexpected behavior.

content.intro: Database correctness depends on more than constructing a query. Use PDO prepared statements for values, database constraints for integrity, transactions for related changes, and bounded queries for predictable performance. In this lesson, focus on create records; then compare it with read records. Use the example to predict a result before checking it, and record one case where the behavior may differ.
content.why_it_matters: You will use crud operations when building readable, testable PHP programs. Its practical value is knowing which rule applies, what result to expect, and how to handle failure or unexpected input.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Database correctness depends on more than constructing a query. Use PDO prepared statements for values, database constraints for integrity, transactions for related changes, and bounded queries for predictable performance. For crud operations, begin with create records. Also distinguish read records; update records; delete records. Identify the input, the rule applied, and the observable output or side effect; then check the relevant official reference when a version or edge-case detail matters.

common_mistakes.why: Input can change the meaning of a query.
common_mistakes.fix: Use PDO prepared statements and bind values separately from the query text.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming application checks are enough for data integrity.
common_mistakes.why: Concurrent requests can race and bypass check-then-write assumptions.
common_mistakes.fix: Use unique constraints, foreign keys, transactions, and appropriate locking.

common_mistakes.why: Memory and response time can grow unexpectedly.
common_mistakes.fix: Use filtering and bounded pagination or streaming for large results.
